theory.intro: **Straight-line depreciation** takes the same dollar amount off an asset's value every period, so the value falls in equal steps. The **salvage value** left after $n$ periods is $S = V_{0} - Dn$.
facts: In $S = V_{0} - Dn$, $S$ is the salvage value, $V_{0}$ the initial value, $D$ the loss per period and $n$ the periods.
The same dollar amount is lost each period, so a graph of value against time is a straight line.
To write an asset down to zero over $n$ years, use $0=V_0-Dn$, so $D=V_0\div n$.
A rate given as a percentage **of the purchase price** is a fixed dollar amount: $8\%$ of $\$50\,000$ is $\$4000$ every year.
The total depreciation after $n$ periods is $Dn$, and the value left over is $V_{0} - Dn$.

For a positive initial value and depreciation amount, straight-line value reaches zero after $n=\dfrac{V_0}{D}$ periods. Stop this model at zero. With a fixed declining-balance rate greater than $0\%$ and less than $100\%$, a positive value decreases but does not reach zero.
When the method changes from straight-line to declining-balance depreciation, use the value at the end of the straight-line stage as the initial value for the declining-balance stage.
steps: Identify the known values and the unknown. Use the same period for $D$ and $n$.
Evaluate, or rearrange to find the unknown. Round as asked.
For two stages, calculate the value after the first stage, then apply the second method for the remaining years.

workedExamples.question_text: A car costs $\$28\,000$ and depreciates by $\$3400$ each year using the straight-line method. Find its value after $3$ years.
A computer costs $\$6600$. Find the annual straight-line depreciation amount needed for it to be worth zero after $8$ years.
A machine costs $\$48\,000$. Using straight-line depreciation, it loses $12.5\%$ of its purchase price each year. After how many years will its value be $\$30\,000$?
workedExamples.solution_text:
Annual depreciation:
$\begin{aligned}D&=0.125\times48000\\D&=\$6000\end{aligned}$
Find the time:
$\begin{aligned}S&=V_0-Dn\\30000&=48000-6000n\\6000n&=18000\\n&=3\end{aligned}$
The value is $\$30\,000$ after $3$ years.

(a) The value falls from $\$18\,000$ at $n=0$ to $\$15\,000$ at $n=1$.
$\begin{aligned}D&=18000-15000\\D&=\$3000\end{aligned}$
The annual loss is $\$3000$.
(b) At $n=4$, read $S=\$6000$.
Check using the formula:
$\begin{aligned}S&=18000-3000(4)\\S&=\$6000\end{aligned}$

workedExamples.question_text: An asset costs $\$75\,000$. For the first $4$ years it depreciates by $\$8200$ per year using the straight-line method. It then depreciates at $20\%$ per annum using the declining-balance method. Find its value after $7$ years and its total depreciation over those years.
workedExamples.solution_text:
Value after the first $4$ years:
$\begin{aligned}S&=V_0-Dn\\S&=75000-8200(4)\\S&=\$42\,200\end{aligned}$
Remaining time $=7-4=3$ years.
Value after another $3$ years:
$\begin{aligned}S&=V_0(1-r)^n\\S&=42200(0.8)^3\\S&=\$21\,606.40\end{aligned}$
Total depreciation:
$\begin{aligned}&\mathrel{\phantom{=}}75000-21606.40\\&=\$53\,393.60\end{aligned}$

workedExamples.question_text: Equipment costs $\$40\,000$. It can be depreciated using either straight-line depreciation of $\$3000$ per year or declining-balance depreciation at $10\%$ per annum. Which method gives the lower salvage value after $3$ years? Justify your answer with calculations.
workedExamples.solution_text:
Straight-line method:
$\begin{aligned}S&=V_0-Dn\\S&=40000-3000(3)\\S&=\$31\,000\end{aligned}$
Declining-balance method:
$\begin{aligned}S&=V_0(1-r)^n\\S&=40000(0.9)^3\\S&=\$29\,160\end{aligned}$
The declining-balance method gives the lower salvage value because $29160<31000$.

mastery.question_text:
Equipment costs $\$84\,000$. It can be depreciated using either straight-line depreciation of $\$9000$ per year or declining-balance depreciation at $15\%$ per annum.
Which method gives the lower salvage value after $4$ years? Justify your answer with calculations and give money amounts to the nearest cent.
mastery.solution_text:
Straight-line method:
$S=V_0-Dn$
$=84000-9000(4)$
$=\$48\,000$.
Declining-balance method:
$S=V_0(1-r)^n$
$=84000(0.85)^4$
$=\$43\,848.525$
$\approx\$43\,848.53$.
The declining-balance method gives the lower salvage value because $43848.53<48000$.
